sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... LITTLE CHANGE TO THE LARGE-SCALE PATTERN IS FORECAST WITH A LONG-WAVE TROUGH OVER ERN NORTH AMERICA...DOWNSTREAM FROM A LOW OVER THE GULF OF AK AND RIDGE CENTERED ACROSS THE FOUR CORNERS REGION. A BELT OF ENHANCED MIDLEVEL FLOW WILL EXIST BETWEEN THESE TWO LATTER FEATURES FROM THE CANADIAN ROCKIES AND PACIFIC NW THROUGH THE NRN/CNTRL PLAINS INTO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES AND OH VALLEY. SEVERAL MIDLEVEL PERTURBATIONS --SOME OF CONVECTIVE ORIGIN-- ARE EMBEDDED WITHIN THIS HIGHER MOMENTUM AIR STREAM WITH THESE FEATURES CONTRIBUTING TO ONGOING TSTMS FROM THE NRN HIGH PLAINS TO MID SOUTH. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE SEWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY WITH THE WRN EXTENSION OF THIS FRONT SETTLING MORE SLOWLY SWD THROUGH THE MID MS VALLEY AND CNTRL PLAINS IN TANDEM WITH A LEE CYCLONE OVER WRN KS. SEVERAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES ARE PRESENT TO THE SOUTH AND EAST OF THE SYNOPTIC FRONT FROM THE CNTRL PLAINS INTO THE OH VALLEY WITH ALL OF THESE SURFACE DISCONTINUITIES POTENTIALLY SERVING AS GENESIS REGIONS FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT TODAY.

sections.title: KS/OK INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY/MID SOUTH TODAY INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: A COMPLEX FORECAST SCENARIO EXISTS THIS MORNING OWING TO THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE MCSS AND DISPERSIVE MODEL SOLUTIONS. THE STRONGEST AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION IS EXPECTED OCCUR ALONG THE WRN/SWRN FLANK OF ONGOING STORMS WHERE THE COLOCATION OF VERY STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND RICH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WILL YIELD AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 2000-4000+ J/KG. LOW-LEVEL UPLIFT ALONG THE SYNOPTIC FRONT AND EXISTING CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS WILL BE AUGMENTED BY DCVA ATTENDANT TO A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH PROGRESSING SEWD INTO THE MID MO VALLEY TO SUSTAIN A SUBSET OF ONGOING STORMS THROUGH THE DAY...AS WELL AS FOSTER ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON. THE STRONGEST DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL RESIDE ACROSS KS PORTION OF SLIGHT RISK WHERE SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE. OTHERWISE...EXPECT THE PREFERRED STORM MODE TO BE BOWING CONVECTIVE SYSTEMS CAPABLE OF PRIMARILY DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING
sections.text: SIMILAR TO MONDAY...THE STATIONARY FRONT/INVERTED TROUGH AND TERRAIN-INDUCED CIRCULATIONS ARE EXPECTED TO FOSTER WIDELY SCATTERED TSTM DEVELOPMENT BY MID TO LATE AFTERNOON. THE COMBINATION OF MODERATE INSTABILITY AND 40-50 KT OF DEEP NWLY SHEAR WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING
sections.text: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT RATHER STRONG DAYTIME HEATING SHOULD OCCUR AHEAD OF THE FRONT...AND WHEN COMBINED WITH A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER...WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AFTERNOON AIR MASS WITH MLCAPE APPROACHING 1000-2000 J/KG. MIDLEVEL HEIGHT FALLS/DCVA ASSOCIATED WITH THE SHORT-WAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS THE REGION WILL ENHANCE DEEP-LAYER ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT WITH SCATTERED STORMS DEVELOPING. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE MARGINALLY SUPPORTIVE OF STORM ORGANIZATION...WITH A MIXTURE OF LINE SEGMENTS AND MULTICELLS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND SOME HAIL INTO THIS EVENING.

sections.title: LOWER HUDSON VALLEY INTO SRN NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THE 12Z SOUNDING FROM NEW YORK CITY INDICATES PRESENCE OF A VERY MOIST AIR MASS WHICH IS ALREADY CONTRIBUTING TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS TO THE SOUTH OF THE STALLED SYNOPTIC FRONT. CONVERGENCE ALONG THIS BOUNDARY WILL COMBINE WITH INCREASED FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH APPROACHING FROM THE WEST TO PROMOTE SCATTERED TSTMS TODAY...A FEW OF WHICH COULD BE STRONG TO MARGINALLY SEVERE WITH DAMAGING WINDS BEING THE PRIMARY HAZARD. ..MEAD/MOSIER.. 07/23/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SOME AMPLIFICATION OF THE WESTERLIES IS ONGOING...CENTERED NEAR THE CANADIAN/U.S. BORDER AREA. WHILE UPPER RIDGING BECOMES MORE PROMINENT ACROSS THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST AND BRITISH COLUMBIA THROUGH ALBERTA AND THE NORTHERN U.S. ROCKIES...BROADLY CYCLONIC UPPER FLOW CONTINUES TO EVOLVE EAST OF THE PLAINS INTO THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD. A NUMBER OF SHORT WAVE IMPULSES ARE PROGRESSING THROUGH THIS LATTER REGIME...THE MOST SIGNIFICANT OF WHICH IS NOW DIGGING ACROSS EASTERN ONTARIO...BEFORE GRADUALLY TURNING EASTWARD INTO QUEBEC LATER TODAY AND TONIGHT. THIS FEATURE IS ACCOMPANIED BY A SIGNIFICANT COLD FRONT...WHICH IS EXPECTED TO ADVANCE SOUTH AND EAST OF THE GREAT LAKES REGION...INTO THE OHIO VALLEY/NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC COAST AND NEW ENGLAND BY 12Z WEDNESDAY. EAST OF THE ROCKIES...WHERE 70F SURFACE DEW POINTS REMAIN COMMON ACROSS THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN PLAINS...INTO THE OHIO VALLEY AND GULF/SOUTH ATLANTIC COASTS...VERY WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR CONTINUES TO ADVECT EAST SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS...TOWARD THE OHIO VALLEY. THIS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO LARGE CAPE...AND THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES POTENTIALLY SUPPORTIVE OF SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT OVER A SIZABLE AREA...IN THE PRESENCE OF

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS INTO THE VICINITY OF THE APPALACHIANS
sections.text: THE COLD FRONT ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES APPEARS PRECEDED BY DRYING IN THE WAKE OF A LEADING WIND SHIFT/CONVECTIVELY GENERATED BOUNDARY NOW CURVING ACROSS NORTH CENTRAL INDIANA AND CENTRAL ILLINOIS THROUGH THE INTERSTATE 70 CORRIDOR OF MISSOURI. ANOTHER CONVECTIVELY GENERATED BOUNDARY APPEARS TO HAVE ADVANCED SOUTHWARD ACROSS MUCH OF NORTHERN AND CENTRAL KANSAS. ADDITIONALLY...OVERNIGHT CONVECTION HAS LEFT A SIZABLE COLD/STABLE SURFACE BUBBLE ACROSS MUCH OF SOUTHEAST MISSOURI/NORTHWESTERN ARKANSAS AND ADJACENT WESTERN KENTUCKY/TENNESSEE AND NORTHERN MISSISSIPPI. OUTSIDE OF THIS LATTER FEATURE...AND SOUTH OF THE PRE-FRONTAL BOUNDARIES...DAYTIME HEATING IS EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO CAPE OF 2000-3000+ J/KG. MODELS CONTINUE TO SUGGEST THE SOUTHEASTWARD DEVELOPMENT OF AN AREA OF LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION...NOW ASSOCIATED WITH WEAK CONVECTION OVER THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY... THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE PERIOD. SPECIFICS REMAIN UNCLEAR... BUT THE ENVIRONMENT STILL APPEARS CONDUCIVE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF ADDITIONAL CONVECTION...AND UPSCALE GROWTH INTO ONE OR MORE ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS...ACROSS PARTS OF KANSAS/OKLAHOMA AND MISSOURI THROUGH THE OZARK PLATEAU AND ADJ

sections.title: NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: RESIDUAL LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IN A SOUTHEASTERLY UPSLOPE REGIME...BENEATH NORTHWESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW...COUPLED WITH STEEPENING LAPSE RATES ARE STILL EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR AT LEAST SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE STORMS LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. THIS PROBABLY WILL INCLUDE A COUPLE OF SUPERCELLS AND ONE OR TWO SMALL ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS.

sections.title: GREAT BASIN
sections.text: CONVECTION EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ALONG A SLOWLY NORTHWARD ADVANCING SHEAR AXIS LIKELY WILL BE PRECEDED BY THE DEVELOPMENT OF A VERY WARM/HOT...DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS MUCH OF CENTRAL/ SOUTHERN UTAH INTO PARTS OF EASTERN NEVADA. THIS ENVIRONMENT PROBABLY WILL BE CONDUCIVE TO THE RISK FOR AT LEAST LOCALIZED STRONG CONVECTIVE SURFACE GUSTS LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.title: LONG ISLAND AREA INTO SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: VIGOROUS CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT STILL APPEARS POSSIBLE NEAR A WEAK SURFACE LOW...WITHIN THE LEE SURFACE TROUGH...MIGRATING NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE REGION THIS AFTERNOON. DEEP LAYER LAPSE RATES ARE RATHER WEAK...AND FLOW FIELDS...PARTICULARLY AT LOWER/MID-LEVELS...SEEM MARGINAL AT BEST. HOWEVER...PRECIPITABLE WATER IS HIGH...AND IT MAY NOT BE OUT OF THE QUESTION THAT HEAVY PRECIPITATION LOADING COULD CONTRIBUTE TO STRONG WIND GUSTS NEAR STRONGER CONVECTION. ..KERR/LEITMAN.. 07/23/2013

sections.title: DIXIE
sections.text: UPSCALE ORGANIZATION OF CONVECTION OVER NRN PORTIONS MS/AL HAS LED TO WELL-ORGANIZED QLCS MOVING SEWD INTO FAVORABLY MOIST/HEATED/UNSTABLE AIR MASS...WITH POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING GUSTS AND SPORADIC SVR HAIL POTENTIALLY EXTENDING AS FAR S AS GULF COAST BY LATE AFTN OR EARLY EVENING. REF SPC WW 436 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE ON THIS SITUATION.

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO LOWER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: BKN BAND OF STG-SVR TSTMS...WITH BOTH WIND AND HAIL RISK...HAS DEVELOPED ALONG PREFRONTAL CONFLUENCE/WIND-SHIFT LINE...FROM NERN OH SWWD ACROSS SRN INDIANA. THIS ACTIVITY WILL MOVE INTO SFC AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY DEW POINTS UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S F...SUPPORTING PRECONVECTIVE MLCAPE RANGING FROM AROUND 1000 J/KG OVER WRN PA TO 3000 J/KG IN SRN INDIANA WHERE DEEP-LAYER LAPSE RATES ARE HIGHER. REF WW 435 AND ACCOMPANYING MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST DEVELOPMENTS IN EVOLUTION OF THIS THREAT.

sections.title: SERN NY...NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS WILL CONTINUE TO OFFER THREAT FOR SPORADIC ISOLATED SVR HAIL AND DAMAGING GUSTS FOR REMAINDER AFTN..ALONG AND AHEAD OF SFC TROUGH AND CONFLUENCE LINE THAT IS MOVING EWD ACROSS THIS REGION INTO AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY WEAK CINH AND 70S F SFC DEW POINTS. REF MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1481 FOR MORE DETAILS.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS TO OZARKS
sections.text: SLGT SWD SHIFT HAS BEEN MADE TO OUTLOOK LINES IN DEFERENCE TO BOUNDARY/INSTABILITY TRENDS. REF SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1483...AS WELL AS WW 437 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS...FOR THIS CORRIDOR. ..EDWARDS.. 07/23/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1125 AM CDT TUE JUL 23 2013/

sections.title: KS/OK/SWRN MO/NWRN-WRN AR
sections.text: LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING SURFACE ANALYSES SHOWED A BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM SRN MO WWD INTO FAR NERN OK AND THEN WNWWD THROUGH SOUTH CENTRAL KS /BETWEEN KICT AND KP28/ TO AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE IN SWRN KS. OBJECTIVE ANALYSES AND 00Z SOUNDINGS OVER THIS SLIGHT RISK AREA INDICATED THE ENVIRONMENT REMAINS VERY STRONGLY TO EXTREMELY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE RANGING FROM 3000-4000 J/KG. VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILES ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE SURFACE BOUNDARY AS SAMPLED BY THE 00Z OUN SOUNDING AND OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATED EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 35-50 KT OVER KS/OK. A STRENGTHENING SLY LLJ FROM WRN TX INTO OK IS EXPECTED TO VEER OVERNIGHT. THESE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMICS...PW NEAR 2 INCH AT 00Z OUN SOUNDING...AND SUFFICIENT BULK SHEAR SUGGEST THE ONGOING STORMS OVER CENTRAL/SRN KS HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO SPREAD SWD INTO THE REST OF SRN KS AND OK. DAMAGING WINDS...SOME SIGNIFICANT...AND LARGE HAIL...SOME VERY LARGE...REMAIN A LIKELY THROUGH TONIGHT /WELL AFTER DARK/.

sections.title: PART OF SRN GA INTO NWRN FL AND THE ERN FL PANHANDLE
sections.text: PRIOR TO THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZING...ADDITIONAL DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE AS THE LEADING EDGE OF AN MCS SPREADS E/SEWD THROUGH THIS REGION.

sections.title: PART OF WRN NEB INCLUDING THE PANHANDLE TO DAKOTAS
sections.text: RESIDUAL MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT SUGGEST AT LEAST THE LONE STORM OVER WEST CENTRAL NEB WILL PERSIST SSEWD THROUGH SWRN NEB AND MAY REACH NWRN KS.

sections.title: SRN NEW ENGLAND TO LONG ISLAND
sections.text: OVERALL ISOLATED SVR WEATHER THREAT HAS DIMINISHED ACROSS THIS REGION AS STORMS HAVE EITHER MOVED OFFSHORE...AND/OR THE BOUNDARY LAYER IN ADVANCE OF ANY REMAINING STORMS WILL FURTHER STABILIZE LIMITING TSTM DEVELOPMENT/INTENSITY. ..PETERS.. 07/24/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A MARGINAL SEVERE HAIL/WIND THREAT MAY EXIST FOR THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...WITH SUBSTANTIAL TSTM COVERAGE/INTENSITY PROBABLY HOLDING OFF UNTIL LATER THIS MORNING/AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: PRESENCE OF VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES IS EVIDENT BEHIND AND AHEAD OF ELEVATED TSTM CLUSTERS FROM THE LOWER MO VALLEY INTO CNTRL KS. 12Z TOP/LBF RAOBS BOTH SAMPLED 700-500 MB LAPSE RATES OF 9 DEG C/KM. LACK OF STRONG DEEP-LAYER FLOW APPEARS TO BE THE PRIMARY LIMITING FACTOR TO A MORE ORGANIZED CLUSTER WITH EFFECTIVE SHEAR AROUND 20 KT PER TOP/OAX RAOBS. ALTHOUGH CURRENT TIME OF DAY IS NOT CONDUCIVE TO A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN CONVECTIVE INTENSITY...ROBUST DOWNSTREAM HEATING WILL OCCUR SHORTLY AND THERE IS CONCERN FOR AT LEAST A MARGINAL SEVERE RISK PERSISTING THROUGH THE MORNING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CLUSTER OF STORMS OVER NRN MS IS BEING MONITORED FOR UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS AND INCREASING DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL. WW IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR IMAGERY AT 1445Z SHOWED A CLUSTER OF THUNDERSTORMS MOVING ESEWD AT 40 KT OVER NRN MS...WHILE A SECOND COLD POOL AND ASSOCIATED CONVECTION WAS SURGING SWD OVER FAR NWRN MS AND E-CNTRL AR. ANOTHER AREA OF CONVECTION WAS ALSO MOVING EWD OVER NRN/CNTRL AL...AND HAS LEFT AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY IN ITS WAKE FROM ROUGHLY CBM SEWD TO 20 N OF TOI. MEANWHILE...CLEAR SKIES OVER CNTRL MS COMBINED WITH WLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW IS AIDING IN STRONG SURFACE HEATING. THE DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER AIRMASS COMBINED WITH LOW TO MID 70 DEWPOINTS IS YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES FROM 1500-2500 J/KG. THIS AIRMASS WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT AS THE COLD POOL OVER NRN MS MOVES SWD INTO CNTRL MS AND W-CNTRL AL. AS THIS TAKES PLACE...UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS AND SUBSEQUENT INCREASE IN DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL MAY OCCUR...AND COULD NECESSITATE THE NEED FOR A WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS AND SMALL LINE SEGMENTS ARE FORECAST TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS MUCH OF OH AND NERN KY...WITH ACTIVITY EVENTUALLY SPREADING EWD INTO WRN PA AND NWRN WV. WW MAY BECOME NECESSARY THIS AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MIDDAY MESOANALYSIS SHOWS A SURFACE COLD FRONT EXTENDING SWWD FROM SRN ONTARIO INTO CNTRL IND AND IL. THETA-E AXIS RESIDES IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE FRONT WHERE TEMPERATURES IN THE 80S ARE COLLOCATED WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S. DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER IS AIDING IN DEEPENING CUMULUS FROM CNTRL OH INTO NERN KY...WITH SEVERAL LIGHTNING STRIKES RECENTLY OCCURRING IN SWRN OH. THIS SHOULD GIVE WAY TO VIGOROUS CONVECTION AS FRONT AND MIDLEVEL IMPULSE OBSERVED IN WV IMAGERY ENCOUNTER A MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS. DEEP-LAYER WLY FLOW INCREASING FROM 20 KT AT 1 KM AGL TO 40 KT AT 6 KM AGL WILL FAVOR MULTICELL CLUSTERS AND SMALL LINES POSING A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. AS THE AFTERNOON PROGRESSES...THETA-E ADVECTION INTO WRN PA AND NWRN WV WILL YIELD AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR MAINTAINING STRONG/SEVERE STORMS MOVING EWD OUT OF OH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE WEATHER THREAT IN THE FORM OF LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH STORMS SPREADING ACROSS SERN LOWER MI. THREAT WILL COME TO AN END AS ACTIVITY MOVES OVER THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER. WW IS UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS HAVE DEVELOPED INVOF A SURFACE COLD FRONT...AND COINCIDENT WITH THE PASSAGE OF A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE. ENVIRONMENT IS CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPERATURES IN THE MID 70S TO LOW 80S...DEWPOINTS NEAR 70...AND MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES AROUND -10C...WHICH IS AIDING IN MODERATE INSTABILITY. DEEP-LAYER WLY FLOW WITH 0-6 KM BULK SHEAR NEAR 30 KT WILL SUPPORT A FEW ORGANIZED CELLS POSING AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. GIVEN THE LOCALIZED AND RELATIVELY BRIEF NATURE OF THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT...A WW DOES NOT APPEAR NECESSARY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS FORECAST TO OCCUR THIS AFTERNOON ALONG AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY OVER CNTRL AR/S-CNTRL MO...AND WITHIN VERY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR AIRMASS LOCATED ACROSS ERN OK/WRN AR AND SWRN MO. CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MORNING CONVECTION CURRENTLY MOVING SWD ACROSS THE LOWER MS VALLEY HAS LEFT BEHIND AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY THAT ARCS NWWD FROM CNTRL MS INTO CNTRL AR...AND THEN NWD INTO S-CNTRL MO. AIRMASS W OF THIS BOUNDARY IS VERY HOT AND MOIST...WITH TEMPERATURES IN THE 90S AND DEWPOINTS GENERALLY IN THE LOW 70S. RESULTANT HIGH THETA-E AIRMASS COMBINED WITH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES IS YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 3000 J/KG. STRONG HEATING IS ALSO ERODING RESIDUAL STABLE LAYER ATOP THE HOT/MOIST SURFACE AIRMASS...WITH CUMULUS FIELD BEGINNING TO SHOW SIGNS OF DEEPENING FROM SWRN MO INTO WRN/CNTRL AR. THESE TRENDS ARE FORECAST TO GIVE WAY TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR AS THE AFTERNOON PROGRESSES. DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PROFILES ARE NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG...BUT THE VERY FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT PULSE AND MULTICELL CLUSTER STORMS POSING A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING DOWNBURSTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS WILL CONTINUE SPREADING EWD THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS NRN NJ...SERN NY/LONG ISLAND...MA...CT...AND RI. ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND SMALL HAIL MAY ACCOMPANY A FEW OF THE STRONGER STORMS...BUT THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT DOES NOT APPEAR TO WARRANT A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WEAK AREA OF SURFACE LOW PRESSURE ASSOCIATED WITH A LOW AMPLITUDE UPPER TROUGH WAS ANALYZED EARLY THIS AFTERNOON DRIFTING ENEWD ACROSS SRN NEW ENGLAND...WITH A SURFACE PRESSURE TROUGH EXTENDING SWWD INTO THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION. CLEARING SKIES DURING THE PAST FEW HOURS HAVE AIDED IN BOOSTING SURFACE TEMPERATURES INTO THE MID 70S TO MID 80S AMIDST A MOIST AIRMASS WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S. AS A RESULT...MLCAPE VALUES HAVE INCREASED TO 500-1500 J/KG ACROSS THE AREA...WHICH HAS AIDED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS. AT 1845Z...ONE BAND OF STORMS WAS MOVING E OFF OF THE APPALACHIANS AND INTO SERN NY/NRN NJ...WHILE A SECOND BAND ORIENTED W-E WAS LOCATED OVER CT/MA. DEEP-LAYER FLOW IS GENERALLY OUT OF THE WSW...WITH SPEEDS INCREASING FROM 30 KT AT 6 KM AGL TO 60 KT AT 12 KM AGL...PER AREA VWP/S AND RAP FORECAST SOUNDINGS. THIS WIND PROFILE COMBINED WITH WEAK TO MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL SUPPORT ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE MULTICELL CLUSTERS POSING A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND SMALL HAIL. THREAT WILL LIKELY WANE AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER COOLS THIS EVENING AND THE UPPER TROUGH EXITS THE REGION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: FORWARD PROPAGATING QLCS WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AS IT SPREADS SSEWD INTO PORTIONS OF SRN MS/AL THIS AFTERNOON...AND EVENTUALLY THE WRN FL PANHANDLE THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 1920Z...LEADING EDGE OF QLCS ARCED SWWD FROM 5 W OF ANB TO MEI...AND THEN WNW TO 30 N OF JAN...AND WAS MOVING SEWD AT 30 KT. AIRMASS AHEAD OF THE QLCS HAS EXPERIENCED STRONG HEATING...WITH TEMPERATURES NEAR 90F...AND WHEN COMBINED WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW TO MID 70S...IS YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 2000 J/KG. MEANWHILE...COLD POOL HAS BECOME WELL PRONOUNCED...WITH TEMPERATURES IN THE WAKE OF THE LEADING LINE OF STORMS RESIDING IN THE LOW 70S. MIDLEVEL NWLY FLOW NEAR 30 KT WILL AID IN CONTINUED COLD POOL ELONGATION SSEWD INTO THE DOWNSTREAM WARM/UNSTABLE AIRMASS. ENVIRONMENT WILL FAVOR EFFICIENT DEVELOPMENT OF NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG THE GUST FRONT...AND SUPPORT A SWATH OF STRONG/SEVERE DOWNBURST WINDS AS ACTIVITY ENTERS SRN MS/AL THIS AFTERNOON...AND THE WRN FL PANHANDLE THIS EVENING. ..GARNER.. 07/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS MAY DEVELOP AND QUICKLY INTENSIFY BY 21-22Z ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL/SE KS. LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS AS THEY GENERALLY TRACK S/SE TOWARD NE OK AND FAR SW MO/NW AR INTO THE EARLY EVENING. TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POTENTIAL WATCH ISSUANCE IN THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS MAY INITIATE BY 21-22Z IN THE VICINITY OF A COLD FRONT ACROSS CNTRL KS...AND/OR AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY NEAR THE SE KS/NE OK BORDER. TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED INTO THE LOW TO MID 90S...AND 19Z MESOANALYSIS INDICATED RAPIDLY WEAKENING INHIBITION. GIVEN STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY ACROSS THE MCD AREA...THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD BE QUITE VIGOROUS ONCE INITIATION OCCURS. EVOLUTION OF ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP IS A BIT UNCLEAR AS STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL STAY JUST NORTH OF THE REGION. HOWEVER...STEEP LAPSE RATES AND INCREASING BULK SHEAR SHOULD BE ADEQUATE TO COMPENSATE FOR WEAKER FORCING ALOFT. CURRENT THINKING IS A S/SE MOVING STORM CLUSTER WILL EVENTUALLY CONGEAL INTO A BOWING SEGMENT ACROSS SRN KS AND MOVE INTO OK/SW MO/NW AR. FURTHER WEST...ACROSS PARTS OF S-CNTRL KS...STORM DEVELOPMENT MAY REMAIN MORE ISOLATED WHERE FORCING IS WEAKER STILL...AND MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES ARE WARMER. LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP INTO THIS EVENING. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WATCH ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS ONGOING FROM SRN IN INTO CNTRL/NERN OH WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. ACTIVITY IS FORECAST TO EVENTUALLY IMPACT PORTIONS OF NRN KY INTO NWRN WV AND WRN PA LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: HOT/MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AIRMASS WAS OBSERVED OVER THE MID/UPPER OH VALLEY AT 1945Z...AND IS YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 1000 J/KG IN ERN OH TO 2500 J/KG OVER SRN IN. THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS CONTINUE TO THRIVE IN THIS ENVIRONMENT AHEAD OF A SURFACE COLD FRONT. ACTIVITY IN OH APPEARS TO BE TIED TO A MIDLEVEL DISTURBANCE MOVING E ACROSS THE STATE. UPPER SUPPORT WITH THIS DISTURBANCE COMBINED WITH CONTINUED BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION OVER WRN PA WILL AID IN STORM MAINTENANCE AS CONVECTION IN OH CROSSES THE STATE LINE. AS A RESULT...SEVERE THREAT SHOULD INCREASE OVER PA DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. IN ADDITION...SURFACE WINDS ARE SLIGHTLY BACKED OUT OF THE SSW...WHICH MAY AUGMENT LOW-LEVEL SHEAR SUFFICIENTLY FOR THE OCCURRENCE OF BRIEF UPDRAFT ROTATION. ACTIVITY TRAILING BACK INTO SWRN OH AND SRN IND IS PROPAGATING SSEWD INTO A THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPERATURES IN THE UPPER 80S...DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S...AND MLCAPE VALUES UPWARDS OF 2500 J/KG. THIS THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT COMBINED WITH 25-30 KT OF DEEP-LAYER WLY SHEAR WILL CONTINUE TO MAINTAIN A SEVERE THREAT AS ACTIVITY APPROACHES PORTIONS OF NRN KY AND NWRN WV LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING. ..GARNER.. 07/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SOME SVR THREAT MAY MOVE E OF WW 435 INTO THIS EVENING...AND THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CLUSTERS OF THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE ADVANCING EWD/ESEWD ACROSS WW 435...WITH THIS ACTIVITY EXPECTED TO BE MOVING E OF WW 435 THROUGH THIS EVENING ESPECIALLY AFTER 2230Z-2300Z. HOWEVER...BEFORE THAT TIME...A QLCS WITH EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENTS WILL ADVANCE ACROSS PARTS OF N-CNTRL PA -- AIDED BY A LONGER-LIVED MCV -- AND POTENTIALLY SUPPORT A DMGG WIND THREAT JUST OUTSIDE THE WW 435 AREA ACROSS ELK...WARREN...AND MCKEAN COUNTIES. FARTHER S...STORMS WILL LIKELY EXIT WW 435 INTO CNTRL PA AREA LATER THIS EVENING...OWING TO 20-25 KT OF MID-LEVEL FLOW POTENTIALLY SUPPORTING FORWARD-PROPAGATING STORM CLUSTERS ADVANCING INTO AROUND 500-1000 J/KG OF MLCAPE ACROSS CNTRL PA. SOME DMGG WIND POTENTIAL MAY ENSUE. HOWEVER...EVENTUAL NOCTURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION MAY LIMIT OVERALL STORM INTENSITY BY THE TIME CONVECTION EDGES E OF WW 435.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH MAY BE WARRANTED FOR PORTIONS OF WRN SD AND WRN NEB IF ISOLATED SUPERCELLS CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN AREAL COVERAGE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTION HAS GRADUALLY DEEPENED AND INTENSIFIED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WRN SD OVER THE LAST FEW HOURS. AS BOUNDARY LAYER HAS WARMED INHIBITION HAS WEAKENED CONSIDERABLY WHICH SHOULD PROVE FAVORABLE FOR THUNDERSTORMS TO BEGIN SPREADING SEWD OFF THE BLACK HILLS TOWARD NWRN NEB. DEEP NWLY FLOW ALOFT AND SFC-6KM SHEAR ON THE ORDER OF 50KT WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS AND LARGE HAIL. IT/S NOT ENTIRELY CLEAR HOW EXPANSIVE CONVECTIVE THREAT WILL BE THIS EVENING BUT WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR THIS REGION FOR POSSIBLE WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR VERY ISOLATED SVR STORMS WILL EXIST INTO THE EARLY EVENING HOURS...AND THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VERY ISOLATED STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ON EITHER SIDE OF THE RED RIVER FROM CHOCTAW COUNTY OK TO FANNIN COUNTY TX AMIDST WEAK LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND LIMITED MLCINH. ADDITIONAL UPDRAFTS ARE MANIFESTED IN RADAR ECHOES W OF THE CHOCTAW COUNTY ACTIVITY IN FAR SRN OK. STRONG DIURNAL HEATING SUPPORTING SFC TEMPERATURES IN THE MIDDLE/UPPER 90S AMIDST LOWER 70S DEWPOINTS HAS CONTRIBUTED TO AROUND 2500-3500 J/KG OF MLCAPE. THIS MAY CONDITIONALLY SUPPORT INTENSE UPDRAFTS/DOWNDRAFTS WITH LOCALIZED LARGE HAIL/DMGG WINDS. HOWEVER...ANY SUBSTANTIVE TROPOSPHERIC FLOW -- I.E. ABOVE 30 KT -- IS PRIMARILY RELEGATED TO AOA 8 KM AGL. DESPITE CORRESPONDING SUPPORT FOR CONVECTIVE VENTILATION...NOTABLY WEAKER FLOW IS FOUND THROUGH A LARGE DEPTH OF THE CONVECTIVE CLOUD LAYER. AS SUCH...CONVECTION MAY STRUGGLE TO ATTAIN ANY SUBSTANTIAL ORGANIZATION. FURTHERMORE...STORM COVERAGE WILL BE LARGELY SUPPRESSED BY THE LACK OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT...AND CONVECTION SHOULD WEAKEN AFTER SUNSET.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR SVR STORMS CONTINUES ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF WW 435.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: PRE-FRONTAL CONVECTION HAS CONGEALED INTO MULTIPLE CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS FROM WRN PA SWWD INTO ERN OHIO AND PARTS OF WRN KY. THIS ACTIVITY WILL ADVANCE INTO/ACROSS ERN/SRN PARTS OF WW 435 DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...AND COULD POSE A THREAT FOR DMGG WINDS WITH MODERATE INSTABILITY IN PLACE. SVR HAIL CANNOT BE RULED OUT...ESPECIALLY WITH ANY MORE SEMI-DISCRETE CONVECTION THAT REMAINS -- E.G. ACROSS PARTS OF SWRN PA TO THE S OF PITTSBURGH. THIS PRE-FRONTAL ACTIVITY MAY BEGIN TO WEAKEN IN A COUPLE OF HOURS AS NOCTURNAL STABILIZATION INCREASES. ADDITIONAL CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ALONG A SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY IS PRIMARILY RELEGATED TO CENTRAL OHIO FROM THE S SIDE OF THE COLUMBUS METRO AREA TO NEAR SPRINGFIELD. THE PRESENCE OF AROUND 40 KT OF 0-6-KM BULK SHEAR PER WILMINGTON OH VWP DATA SUGGESTS A FEW SUSTAINED STRONGER UPDRAFTS MAY EVOLVE WITH THIS ACTIVITY IN THE NEAR-TERM BEFORE IT WEAKENS OWING TO NOCTURNAL COOLING AND DECREASING PW TRENDS PER GPS DATA. STORMS WILL ALSO CROSS THE NERN OH/NWRN PA LAKESHORE IN THE NEXT HOUR OR SO...BUT MAY WEAKEN AS NOCTURNAL STABILIZATION TAKES PLACE OVER INLAND AREAS. ..COHEN.. 07/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR DMGG WINDS CONTINUES ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF WW 436...WHICH HAS BEEN EXPANDED EWD UPON COORDINATION WITH THE TALLAHASSEE FL WEATHER FORECAST OFFICE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BOW ECHO ARCS FROM SWRN GA SWWD ACROSS FAR SERN AL AND WWD/WSWWD ACROSS THE FL PANHANDLE...FOLLOWED BY A WELL-DEFINED TRANSITION ZONE AND STRATIFORM RAIN REGION. CONVERGENCE AT THE LEADING EDGE OF THE STRONG COLD POOL ASSOCIATED WITH THE LEADING CONVECTIVE LINE WILL LIKELY FOSTER REGENERATIVE CONVECTION ACROSS SWRN GA AND CNTRL PARTS OF THE FL PANHANDLE WHERE MODERATE/STRONG INSTABILITY REMAINS. HIGH PW -- I.E. ABOVE 1.8 INCHES PER GPS DATA -- WILL ENHANCE WATER LOADING AND THE POTENTIAL FOR INTENSE DOWNDRAFTS WITH DMGG WIND GUSTS. THE WW HAS BEEN EXPANDED EWD AS THE CONVECTION CONTINUES TO SPREAD EWD/SWD AT 25-35 KT...IMPACTING PARTS OF SWRN GA AND PARTS OF THE FL PANHANDLE DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. CONVECTION WILL LIKELY WEAKEN THEREAFTER IN RESPONSE TO NOCTURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION. ..COHEN.. 07/23/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SVR POTENTIAL CONTINUES ACROSS WW 437...AND ISOLATED SVR STORMS MAY OCCUR FARTHER E ACROSS THE OHIO RIVER VALLEY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CLUSTERS OF VIGOROUS CONVECTION CONTINUE NEAR AND S OF A FRONTAL ZONE EXTENDING FROM SRN KS INTO SRN MO AND SRN IL/INDIANA. WWD-MOVING OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES ARE EVIDENT ACROSS N-CNTRL AR AND S-CNTRL MO...WITH NEW CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ON THE COOL SIDE OF THE BOUNDARIES. THESE BOUNDARIES MAY ALSO BOOST STORM INTENSITY AS THEY INTERACT WITH SFC-BASED CONVECTION SHIFTING SEWD/SWD OVER NWRN AR. THE MOST UNSTABLE AIR MASS IS CONFINED TO NWRN AR...SWRN MO...AND ADJACENT FAR SERN KS...WHERE CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING HAS BEEN THE LEAST WIDESPREAD THUS FAR AND THE HIGHEST CONDITIONAL SVR POTENTIAL WILL EXIST. OTHERWISE...AT LEAST SOME SVR POTENTIAL WILL REMAIN INTO THE EVENING WITH SVR HAIL/DMGG WIND POSSIBLE WITH MODEST MID-LEVEL FLOW LIKELY FOSTERING MULTICELLULAR CONVECTION. ADDITIONAL CONVECTION DEVELOPING E OF WW 437 NEAR A SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY FROM SERN MO INTO FAR SWRN INDIANA MAY POSE AN ISOLATED SVR THREAT INTO THE EVENING. HOWEVER...THE SPATIOTEMPORAL EXTENT OF ANY SVR POTENTIAL SHOULD BE TOO LIMITED FOR WW ISSUANCE E OF WW 437 AS NOCTURNAL STABILIZATION OCCURS AMIDST FORCING FOR ASCENT. ..COHEN.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS ARE EXPECTED WITH CONVECTION AS IT SPREADS FROM NORTH TO SOUTH ACROSS KS INTO OK.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TWO MAIN CLUSTERS OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS HAVE EVOLVED ACROSS KS THIS EVENING. THE NRN MOST CLUSTER INITIATED NORTH OF A WELL DEFINED SFC BOUNDARY WITHIN WEAK WARM ADVECTION BUT HAS NOW EXPANDED IN AREAL COVERAGE AND LEADING EDGE IS ACCELERATING SWD AT ROUGHLY 30KT NEAR HUT. CONSIDERABLE AMOUNT OF CONVECTION HAS BECOME ORIENTED N-S FROM NW OF SLN...SWD TO NEAR HUT WHICH MAY ULTIMATELY ENHANCE SWD MOVEMENT AS PRECIP SHIELD BEGINS TO EXPAND AND POSSIBLY FORM A COLD POOL. A MUCH SLOWER AND MORE ISOLATED STORM HAS DEVELOPED JUST SE OF DDC WHERE INTENSE SFC HEATING COINCIDED WITH ENHANCED LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE NEAR SFC LOW. THIS STORM IS GRADUALLY EXPANDING AND IS EXPECTED TO PROPAGATE SWD INTO NWRN OK IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING OUTFLOW MAY ACCOMPANY EACH OF THESE CLUSTERS. ..DARROW.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A FEW STORMS COULD PRODUCE LOCALIZED SVR WIND GUSTS INTO THIS EVENING...THOUGH THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED CONVECTION THAT DEVELOPED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN AND AIDED BY OROGRAPHIC ASCENT SHOULD PERSIST DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WEAK MID-LEVEL FLOW PER THE 00Z TUS RAOB AND AREA VWP DATA SUGGEST THAT CONVECTION WILL LARGELY LACK ANY APPRECIABLE ORGANIZATION AND MAY STRUGGLE TO MOVE OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN TOWARD THE LOWER ELEVATIONS/DESERT FLOOR. ONE EXCEPTION MAY BE ACROSS PARTS OF SERN AZ...WHERE SOMEWHAT GREATER CONVECTIVE COVERAGE WITHIN A PLUME OF ENHANCED MID-LEVEL MOISTURE/UPDRAFT-SHELTERING HAS ENCOURAGED MORE ROBUST COLD POOL GROWTH AND ENSUING LEADING-EDGE CONVECTIVE REGENERATION. DCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 800 J/KG ASSOCIATED WITH STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT INTENSE DOWNDRAFTS...WITH A FEW SVR WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE ON A LOCALIZED BASIS. NOCTURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION WILL YIELD A DOWNWARD TREND IN CONVECTIVE INTENSITY AFTER SUNSET.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PERKINS AND CHASE COUNTIES MAY NEED TO BE ADDED TO THE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH IF SUPERCELL MAINTAINS INTENSITY OVER THE NEXT HOUR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ONE PRIMARY SUPERCELL IS DIGGING SEWD ACROSS CNTRL PORTIONS OF WW439. THIS STORM IS MOVING AT ROUGHLY 35KT AND COULD EXIT KEITH COUNTY BY 0230Z. LARGE HAIL IS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT AND PORTIONS OF SWRN NEB MAY NEED TO BE ADDED TO THE WATCH IF THIS STORM DOES NOT WEAKEN. ..DARROW.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SVR THREAT WILL EXIST INTO THE EVENING HOURS...THOUGH THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LARGE MASS OF CONVECTION HAS MATERIALIZED ACROSS SRN AR WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY RICH DEEP-LAYER MOISTURE AND LIMITED MLCINH...AS SAMPLED BY THE 00Z SHV RAOB. WITH A PW VALUE AROUND 1.9 INCHES AND AROUND 2000-2500 J/KG OF MLCAPE BASED ON THIS SOUNDING...ENHANCED CONVERGENCE OVER THE SRN FLANK OF THE COLD POOL CORRESPONDING TO THE CONVECTIVE MASS WILL FAVOR ITS FORWARD PROPAGATION INTO/ACROSS NRN LA FROM SRN AR DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WATER LOADING WILL ENHANCE THE POTENTIAL FOR STRONG DOWNBURSTS WITH THE POSSIBILITY FOR DMGG WIND GUSTS. HOWEVER...WITH LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES BECOMING LESS STEEP IN ASSOCIATION WITH NOCTURNAL COOLING...THIS THREAT IS EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY DECREASE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LARGE PART OF SVR TSTM WATCH 437 WILL BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE ON SCHEDULE AT 03Z...THOUGH THE SVR THREAT COULD PERSIST ACROSS PARTS OF SWRN MO AND FAR SERN KS AFTER 03Z PERHAPS WARRANTING A LOCAL EXTENSION IN TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ACROSS MOST PORTIONS OF WW 437...WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING HAS LARGELY DIMINISHED THE SVR THREAT IN THE NEAR TERM AND THE WW MAY BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE ON SCHEDULE AT 03Z. HOWEVER...A WWD-MOVING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS SWRN MO AND FAR NWRN AR MAY CONTINUE TO BE THE FOCUS FOR NEW CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THE 00Z SGF RAOB SAMPLES AN ENVIRONMENT WITH STRONG BUOYANCY AND MODERATE MID-LEVEL FLOW WHICH COULD YIELD SOME SVR THREAT PERSISTING BEYOND 03Z IN SWRN MO...FAR SERN KS...AND FAR NWRN AR. ALSO...INTENSE CONVECTION UPSTREAM ACROSS KS MAY MOVE ACROSS PARTS OF THE REGION LATER TONIGHT...AND THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE MONITORED FOR ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE LATER TONIGHT. ..COHEN.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: MCS IS EXPECTED TO EXPAND AND SPREAD SEWD OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONSIDERABLE AMOUNT OF CONVECTION HAS EVOLVED ACROSS SRN KS THIS EVENING WITHIN ZONE OF WEAK WARM ADVECTION. EARLIER ACTIVITY THAT INITIATED NEAR THE SFC LOW WITHIN DEEPLY MIXED ENVIRONMENT OVER SWRN KS HAS WEAKENED WITH LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING. AS A RESULT...IT APPEARS THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF STORMS WILL BE FOCUSED ALONG A NW-SE CORRIDOR FROM ROUGHLY ICT-TUL. AN UPWARD EVOLVING MCS WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN AREAL COVERAGE ACROSS SCNTRL/SERN KS OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AND SPREAD INTO NRN/NERN OK. 00Z SOUNDING AT OUN EXHIBITED A VERY UNSTABLE PROFILE WITH MUCAPE IN EXCESS OF 5000 J/KG AND PW VALUES APPROACHING 2 INCHES. VERY DAMAGING WINDS MAY OCCUR WITH LEADING EDGE OF MATURING MCS...IN ADDITION TO LARGE HAIL. ..DARROW.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: NEW SEVERE TSTM WATCH WILL LIKELY BE ISSUED TO SUPERSEDE WW 438 WHICH IS SCHEDULED TO EXPIRE AT 06Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BOWING MCS WHICH RECENTLY PASSED THROUGH THE TULSA METRO AREA HAS HAD A HISTORY OF MEASURED SEVERE WIND GUSTS ALONG THE APEX OF THE BOW /66 KT AT KTUL AND 60-70 MPH GUSTS MEASURED AT A FEW OK-MESONET SITES/. OUTFLOW FROM THE N/S-ORIENTED CLUSTER ALONG THE OK/AR BORDER APPEARS TO HAVE STALLED AND/OR DISSIPATED AROUND 1-2 COUNTIES W OF THE BORDER. CURRENT MOVEMENT OF THE BOW SUGGEST THE THRUST OF THE LINE MAY LARGELY REMAIN ON THE COOL SIDE OF THE BOUNDARY. NEVERTHELESS...WITH SURFACE TEMPERATURES HOLDING IN THE 80S TO THE W OF THE BOUNDARY...A 25 KT SWLY LLJ SAMPLED IN TLX VWP DATA...IT APPEARS PLAUSIBLE THAT ADDITIONAL ROBUST UPDRAFTS WILL FORM ALONG THE WRN FLANK OF THE LINE AND POTENTIALLY YIELD FURTHER COLD POOL DEVELOPMENT TO THE W. PRIMARY THREAT WILL REMAIN DAMAGING WINDS...BUT SEVERE HAIL AND A BRIEF QLCS TORNADO ARE POSSIBLE GIVEN THE MATURE NATURE OF THE MCS INTERACTING WITH THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. ..GRAMS.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND THREAT CONTINUES WITH A SWD-MOVING QLCS IN SERN/E-CNTRL OK. PROBABILITY OF SEVERE TSTM WATCH ISSUANCE DOWNSTREAM INTO NERN TX IS 40 PERCENT BY 09Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MEASURED WIND GUSTS HAVE SUBSIDED INTO THE 40-50 MPH RANGE PER OK-MESONET AND KMLC ASOS WITH QLCS THAT EXTENDED FROM LE FLORE TO POTTAWATOMIE COUNTIES IN OK. SWD-MOVEMENT OF THE ERN PORTION CONTINUES AT AROUND 40-50 KT AND WILL LIKELY SURGE ACROSS THE RED RIVER BETWEEN 08-09Z. MUCH OF THIS SURGE IS OCCURRING ON THE COOL SIDE OF A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM AN EARLIER MCS OVER TEXARKANA ON TUE EVENING. GIVEN PROBABLE LOW-LEVEL STABILIZATION IN THE WAKE OF THE EARLIER MCS...DAMAGING WIND THREAT WILL PROBABLY BE LIMITED E OF A PRX TO SHV LINE. POTENTIAL ALSO EXISTS FOR INCREASING FORWARD-PROPAGATION OF THE WRN PORTION OF THE QLCS GIVEN A 30 KT SWLY LLJ SAMPLED IN TLX/FWS VWP DATA. INTENSE REFLECTIVITY CORES HAVE THUS FAR REMAINED WELL N/NE OF THE SURFACE OUTFLOW...BUT COULD EVENTUALLY ACCELERATE SWD IF THE COLD POOL DEEPENS. ..GRAMS.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: OVERALL SEVERE THREAT APPEARS INCREASINGLY MARGINAL AND SHOULD CONTINUE TO WANE. AN ADDITIONAL WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED BEYOND 11Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EARLIER QLCS WEAKENED SUBSTANTIALLY IN THE PAST HALF HOUR AS IT MOVED ACROSS RED RIVER IN BOTH RADAR REFLECTIVITY AND CG LIGHTNING DETECTIONS. ASSOCIATED GUST FRONT HAS SURGED WELL W OF THIS ACTIVITY INTO WRN OK. WLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW ATOP THE SURFACE COLD DOME IS SUPPORTING WAA AND SUSTENANCE OF RENEWED ELEVATED UPDRAFTS ACROSS N-CNTRL OK. SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY COULD PRODUCE SEVERE HAIL GIVEN LARGE BUOYANCY SAMPLED IN THE 05Z LAMONT RAOB...BUT SHOULD BE MARGINALIZED BY THE DOMINANT CLUSTER MODE. A STRONG WIND GUST OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT...BUT ATTEMPTS AT AN ORGANIZED SWD-MOVING COLD POOL PRODUCING SEVERE WIND GUSTS WILL PROBABLY BE MITIGATED BY SURFACE STABILIZATION IN THE WAKE OF THE INITIAL MCS. ..GRAMS.. 07/24/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
